questions.question_text:
A credit card charges $14.6\%$ p.a. compounded daily and has no interest-free period.
A purchase of $\$400$ is made on $9$ July and the statement is issued on $31$ July. Interest includes both the purchase date and the statement date.
What is the amount owing, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Used $31-9=22$ charged days instead of including both dates to obtain $23$ days.
Subtracted the purchase price and gave the interest charged instead of the amount owing.
Charged no interest despite the stated absence of an interest-free period.

questions.question_text:
A purchase of $\$380$ is made on a credit card with no interest-free period charging $21.9\%$ p.a. compounded daily.
Interest is charged for $16$ days.
What is the amount owing, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Gave the interest charged rather than the total amount owing.
Treated the $16$ days as $16$ monthly periods at $\dfrac{0.219}{12}$ each.
Assumed an interest-free period applies, but this card has none.

questions.question_text:
A credit card charges $18.25\%$ p.a. compounded daily with no interest-free period, from and including the purchase date to and including the statement date of $30$ September.
A purchase of $\$600$ is made on $11$ September and one of $\$200$ on $21$ September.
What is the closing balance, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Added the two purchases and charged no interest at all.
Gave the interest charged instead of the closing balance.
Charged $20$ days of interest on both purchases instead of $10$ days on the second.

questions.question_text:
A credit card charges $25.55\%$ p.a. compounded daily.
A single purchase of $\$1800$ is made and interest is charged for $18$ days.
How much interest is charged, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Gave the total amount owing rather than the interest part of it.
Used simple interest for $18$ days instead of daily compounding.
Charged a full year's interest, $1800 \times 0.2555$, instead of $18$ days.

questions.question_text:
A credit card has no interest-free period. Its only purchase is $\$1740.80$, and interest at $18.25\%$ p.a. is compounded daily for $2$ days before the statement is issued.
There is no opening balance, repayment or fee. The minimum payment is $3\%$ of the closing balance.
What is the minimum payment, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Calculated $3\%$ of the original purchase price and omitted the compound interest from the closing balance.
Calculated $2\%$ of the closing balance instead of the required $3\%$.
Gave the whole closing balance instead of calculating its minimum-payment percentage.

questions.solution_text:
$r=\dfrac{0.1825}{365}=0.0005$.
$FV=1740.80(1.0005)^2$.
Closing balance $\approx\$1742.54$.
Minimum payment $=0.03\times1742.54$.
Minimum payment $\approx\$52.28$.

questions.question_text:
Nadia owes $\$1450$ on a credit card charging $18.25\%$ p.a. compounded daily.
Interest is charged for $25$ days, after which she repays $\$600$.
How much does she owe immediately after the repayment, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Subtracted the repayment but charged no interest for the $25$ days.
Gave the balance before the repayment was subtracted.
Gave the interest charged over the $25$ days rather than the amount still owing.
